description: Toy Box Friends G5-02: multiplying and dividing by 10, 100 and 1,000. Digits ride an elevator in the Place Value Building, which lies down into the usual place value chart; the decimal point stays.

youtube.title: Multiply and Divide by 10, 100 and 1,000 | Powers of Ten for Kids | Grade 5 Math | Toy Box Friends
youtube.description:
Monkey "adds a zero" to $0.35 and sells ten bananas for 35 cents! In the Place Value Building, digits ride an elevator: times 10 moves every digit one place bigger, divide by 10 moves it one place smaller, and the decimal point stays put.
You'll learn: each place is 10 times the place to its right, multiplying and dividing whole numbers and decimals by 10, 100 and 1,000, placeholder zeros, powers of ten and exponents (10² = 100, 10³ = 1,000), and converting meters, centimeters and kilometers.
Try at home: draw a place value chart and slide a paper strip with a number left and right. Ask a grown-up to help with scissors.

do.text: Powers of Ten Elevator
Bananas! Fresh bananas! One banana, thirty-five cents!
I'd like ten bananas, please.
Ten? Times ten is easy. Just add a zero!
That's zero point three five zero dollars.
Thirty-five cents for ten bananas? Deal!
Wait... I just sold ten bananas for the price of one!
Adding a zero didn't work. What really happens when we multiply by ten?
Welcome to the Place Value Building! Each floor is a place.
I'm the elevator operator. Going up!
Start on the ones floor. One unit cube is one.
Ten ones make a rod. That's ten, on the tens floor.
Ten rods make a flat. One hundred, on the hundreds floor.
And ten flats make a big cube: one thousand!
A thousand little cubes! Each one is ten of the one before.
Each place is ten times the place to its right.
Going down, each floor is one tenth. One cube cut into ten slices gives tenths.
Cut a tenth into ten again and you get hundredths. Each floor down is ten times smaller.
Going down! Tenths, then hundredths.
Here's thirty-seven: three tens and seven ones.
Bear, times ten, please! Where will the three go?
Up to the hundreds floor!
Both digits ride up one floor. Three hundreds, seven tens.
The ones floor is empty, so a zero holds the place. Three hundred seventy!
placeholder zero
So the zero didn't just get added. The digits moved up!
Times ten again. That's thirty-seven times one hundred.
Two floors up from where we started: three thousand seven hundred.
Once more: thirty-seven times one thousand.
Three floors up: thirty-seven thousand.
See the pattern? Count the zeros in ten, one hundred and one thousand.
That's how many floors the digits ride: one, two or three.
Fun fact! A blue whale can weigh over one hundred thousand kilograms. That's ten to the fifth.
Mathematicians have a short way to write these. Ten squared means ten times ten.
power of ten
The small number is the exponent. It counts how many tens we multiply.
So what is ten cubed, ten to the third power?
Easy! Ten times three. Ten cubed is thirty!
Hmm, that's ten times three. The exponent means three tens multiplied together.
Oh! Ten times ten times ten. That's one thousand!
And the exponent tells the floors to ride. Four times ten cubed: the four rides up three floors.
Four thousand.
Fun fact: a googol is one followed by one hundred zeros. A nine-year-old boy named it!
Back to Monkey's bananas. Thirty-five cents is zero point three five dollars.
Three tenths and five hundredths. The gold landing is the decimal point.
Times ten! Where do the digits go?
Both ride up one floor. Three ones and five tenths: three point five.
The digits moved. The decimal point stayed right where it was.
the point stays
Now, Monkey's sign. Is zero point three five zero more than zero point three five?
No! A zero at the end of a decimal changes nothing. It's the same amount.
So ten bananas cost three dollars and fifty cents!
Now watch the building. It's going to lie down.
Up the building is left on the chart. Here's the place value chart we always use.
Three point five times ten. Every digit moves one place to the left.
Thirty-five. Left means bigger: each place is ten times more.
Zero point three five times one hundred moves two places.
Thirty-five again! Two places left for two zeros.
Two point seven times one hundred? Two places left.
Two hundred seventy. A zero holds the ones place.
Dividing by ten goes the other way. Each digit moves one place to the right.
divide
Forty-five divided by ten.
Four point five. The digits moved right, the point stayed.
Six divided by one hundred. Two places right.
Zero point zero six. A zero holds the tenths place.
Without that zero, it would say six tenths. Much bigger!
Right. Placeholder zeros keep every digit on the right floor.
Three hundred twenty divided by one thousand. Three places right.
Zero point three two. The last zero isn't needed after the point.
Times ten?
One place bigger!
Divide by ten?
One place smaller!
The point?
Stays put!
Going up, one floor for every ten! Going down, divide and back again!
Once more! Going up, one floor for every ten! Going down, divide and back again!
Powers of ten help with measuring. One meter is one hundred centimeters.
So two and a half meters is two point five times one hundred.
Two places left: two hundred fifty centimeters.
One kilometer is one thousand meters. Fifteen hundred meters is how many kilometers?
Divide by one thousand: three places right. One point five kilometers.
Fun fact: kilo means one thousand. A kilogram is one thousand grams.
And money! Ten pencils at forty-five cents each.
Times ten: one place left. Four dollars and fifty cents.
Not forty-five cents with a zero stuck on the end. Got it!
Challenge time! Three quick rides. Ready?
Zero point zero seven times one thousand.
Three places left: seventy!
Five point two times ten squared.
Ten squared is one hundred. Two places left: five hundred twenty!
Eight thousand divided by ten cubed.
Three places right. Just eight!
Ding ding! You rode every floor.
Question one. What is four point six times ten?
Forty-six. One place left.
Question two. What is fifty-two divided by one hundred?
Zero point five two. Two places right.
Question three. What is ten cubed?
Ten times ten times ten: one thousand.
Question four. Monkey says zero point eight times ten is zero point eight zero. Is he right?
No! That's still zero point eight. The answer is eight.
I've learned my lesson. Move the digits, don't just add a zero!
Let's recap.
Each place is ten times the place to its right.
